<entry id="S02221">
<head-word>קָשֶׁה</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, קָשָׁה f. 
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key> preced.) 
<italic>stiff, hard, difficult, severe; strong</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Sabb. IX (X), 2 שני זייפין מן הק' וכ' (some ed. הקַשׁ) two of the stiffest bristles of the swine; Sabb. 90
<sup>b</sup> מקָשָׁה של חזיר אחת carrying one of the stiff bristles of the swine is punishable. Taan. 20
<sup>b</sup> ק' כארז, v. קָנֶה. B. Bath. 88
<sup>b</sup> ק' עונשן של וכ' the responsibility for fraud in measures is severer than that for incest. Ib. ק' גזל הדיוט וכ' robbing an individual is worse than robbing the altar. Gen. R. s. 26, end ק' היא המחלוקת וכ' strife is as bad as (the sins of) the generation of the flood. Ib. s. 71 ק' היא התפלה וכ' prayer is a powerful factor, for it reversed the divine decree. Taan. 8
<sup>a</sup> שלמודו ק' עליו וכ' to whom his study is as hard as iron. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> (in Chald. dict.) ק' יומא וכ', v. קָשֵׁי. Ex. R. s. 6 היה ק' בעיניהם וכ' it seemed too hard a task for them to give up idolatry; a. v. fr.—Erub. 83
<sup>b</sup> בק' with difficulty, v. נַחַת.—[Num. R. s. 16 end קשה ערפם, v. קְשִׁי.]—
<plural-form>Pl. קָשִׁים, קָשִׁין; קָשׁוֹת</plural-form>. Yeb. 47
<sup>b</sup>, a. e. ק' גרים וכ', v. סַפַּחַת. Sot. 2
<sup>a</sup> ק' לזווגן (Snh. 22
<sup>a</sup> קשה), v. זָוַג. Pes. 118
<sup>a</sup> ק' … כקריעת וכ' the providential support of man is as difficult (wonderful) as the splitting of the Red Sea. Ib. ק' … כפלים וכ' man’s support is twice as hard (painful) as travailing. Ber. 57
<sup>b</sup> (etymolog. play on קישואים) מפני שהם ק' לגוף וכ' because they are as hard on the body as swords. Koh. R. to XII, 7 נבואות ק' hard (evil) prophecies; a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup> מריש … ליכא ק' בעלמא וכ' formerly I thought there was no truth in the world. Ib. איקלע … ק' שמיה he came to a place named Ḳushṭa (Truth); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. קוּשְׁטִין</plural-form>. Targ. Y. Num. XXII, 37 מן ק' (h. text האמנם).—Y. Ḥag II, beg. 77
<sup>a</sup> ק' אתון אמרין דהין וכ' do you (Jews) indeed say that the world is maintained by air?</notes></sense>

<entry id="S02229">
<head-word>קָשַׁט</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) [
<italic>to be straight, strong</italic>,] </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to go in a straight line, to shoot forth</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 12 יש מזיק … וקוֹשֵׁט כחץ some demon flies like a bird and shoots through the air like an arrow; Midr. Till. to Ps. XCI; Yalk. ib. 842 וקוֹשֵׁת; Tanḥ. Naso 23 וקושש (corr. acc.); ed. Bub. 28.—Y. Meg. I, 72
<sup>b</sup> מאיכן ק' הקוֹשֵׁט הזה וכ' whence did this archer shoot (whence did he derive the opinion) that &c. (cmp. יָרָה 
<italic>Hif.</italic>).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to correct</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Mets. 107
<sup>b</sup>, v. infra.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קִישֵּׁט</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to shoot, aim, direct</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Erub. IX (VI), 26 ביבין המְקַשְּׁטִין וכ' ed. Zuck. (Var. המשקטין, המְקַשְׁקְשִׁין, v. קִשְׁקֵשׁ II) gutters which gush under the houses (cmp. קָלַח). Lam. R. to III, 12 מקושטים בה Ar. s. v. קורה, read: מְקַשְּׁטִים (Ar. ed. Koh. מְקוֹשְׁשִׁים; ed. מוֹרִים), v. חֵץ.—Part. pass. מְקוּשָּׁט; f. מְקוּשֶּׁטֶת; 
<plural-form>pl. מְקוּשָּׁטִים, מְקוּשָּׁטִין; מְקוּשָּׁטוֹת</plural-form>. Pesik. R. s. 40 (play on מוריה, with ref. to ירה יירה, Ex. XIX, 13) שהיתה מק' כנגד וכ' it (the holy land) was aimed towards (directly under) the heavenly altar (v. כּוּן); Yalk. Cant. 988. Ib. כשם שגודלת הזו … להיות מקושטים וכ' (not מקושטת) as the hair-dresser dressing the bride puts every ornament in its proper place, so must the words of the Law be aimed, every word in its due place.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (cmp. תקן) 
<italic>to dress, adorn, prepare</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ib. שמְקַשֶּׁטֶת לכלה, v. supra. Gen. R. s. 8 מְקַשֵּׁט כלות he (the Lord) attires brides; Koh. R. to VII, 2. Ib.; Gen. R. s. 18 משקִשְּׁטָהּ וכ' after having fitted her out with twenty-four kinds of ornaments; a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab. Sabb. 25
<sup>b</sup> מטה מוצעת ואשה מק' לתלמיד חכם the scholar’s happiness when the couch is spread and the wife dressed (for the Sabbath). Ib. 153
<sup>a</sup> כשהן מק' in festive dress, opp. מלוכלכין; a. fr.—Trnsf. 
<italic>to set right, correct</italic>. Snh. 18
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to התקוששו וקושו, Zeph. II, 1) קַשֵּׁט … קשט אחרים first correct thyself, then correct others; ib. 19
<sup>a</sup>; B. Bath. 60
<sup>b</sup>; B. Mets. 107
<sup>b</sup> קְשׁוֹט וכ'; Yalk. Jer. 302; Midr. Till. to Ps. LIII אם תרצה לקַשֵּׁט אחרים וכ' if thou wishest to correct others, correct thyself first.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִקְשִׁיט</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to prepare, make ready</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 28 הקב"ה היפך … והִקְשִׁיטָן וכ' the Lord turned day into night and prepared them for visitations; (Yalk. Job 920 והתקינן).</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְקַשֵּׁט</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>

<notes> Gen. R. s. 55 בשביל שתִּתְקַשֵּׁט וכ', v. קוֹשֶׁט; Yalk. ib. 95; Yalk. Ps. 777.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S02235">
<head-word>קשי</head-word>
<head-word>קָשָׁה</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to be stiff, hard, difficult</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ber. I, 2
<sup>c</sup> top קָשְׁתָה על דעתך this is difficult according to (not reconcilable with) thy opinion; ib. למה א"ל קשתה (not קשתיה) why did he say to him, it is difficult?—V. קָשֶׁה.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קִישָּׁה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (קִישְּׁתָה, with לילד or without) 
<italic>to have hard labor in travailing</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. IV, 1 בהמה המְקַשָּׁה לילד וכ' if an animal is in labor, and &c., v. עוּבָּר. Nidd. IV, 4 קִשְּׁתָה שלשה וכ' if she was in pain for three days within eleven days; Tosef. ib. V, 8 קִישֵּׁת, קִשֵּׁת. Ib. 10; a. fr.—[Gen. R. s. 61 שהיו מקשין וכ', read: מקישין, v. נָקַשׁ.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִקְשָׁה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to stiffen, harden</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Nidd. 13
<sup>b</sup> המַקְשֶׁה עצמו וכ' he who causes erection wilfully. Ex. R. s. 11 הרשע הזה ה' את לבו וכ' this wicked (Pharaoh) hardened his heart against the first three signs; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to become hard</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Pes. VI, 35
<sup>b</sup> top שסופו להַקְשׁוֹת which gets hard in the course of time. Shebi. II, 10 אם הִקְשׁוּ וכ' (Y. ed. a. Bart. הוּקְשׁוּ 
<italic>Hof.</italic>) if they became hard (dry) and unfit for man to eat before New Year. (Y. ib. 34
<sup>a</sup> bot. הקשו a. הוקשו).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be severe</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 19, opp. ריתה, v. רָתָה.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hof.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הוּקְשֶׁה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to become hard</italic>, v. supra.</definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be found hard, distasteful</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tanḥ. Sh’laḥ 5; Num. R. s. 16 ה' הדבר והרע וכ' the thing was distasteful to and displeased his father.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְקַשֶּׁה, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Nithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִתְקַשֶּׁה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to suffer severely</italic> (in travailing).</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 84 נִתְקַשֵּׁת אמו וכ' his mother was in hard labor at his birth.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to become hard, stiff</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tosef. Nidd. VI, 4 משׁיִתְקַשּׁוּ, v. קִשְׁקֵשׁ I, a. II. Gen. R. s. 98, a. שׁנִתְקַשֵּׁיתָה, v. קַשְׁיוּת.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to find one’s self in difficulty, to be perplexed, unable to understand</italic> or 
<italic>remember</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 15 beg. נ' משה במעשה וכ' Moses found the work of the candlestick more difficult to understand than &c.; כיון שנ' אמר וכ' when he still could not remember it, the Lord said &c. Ib.
<sup>10</sup>; Tanḥ. B’haʿăl. 6 נִתְקַשֵּׁיתִי לעשותה I could not understand how to do it. Ib. נ' על משה it was too difficult for Moses; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be reluctant, strive against</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tanḥ. Sh’moth 18 כמה נ' יונה שלא וכ' how hard did Jonah strive not to go on his mission. Deut. R. s. 9 מִתְקַשֶּׁה כנגדו (the sun) refused to obey; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—5)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to make one’s self obnoxious</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 61; Yalk. Chr. 1073 (play on יקשן, Gen. XXV, 2) שהיו מִתְקַשִּׁין בעולם they were obnoxious to the world (were hard to deal with); (Midr. Till. to Ps. XCII ed. Bub. שהיו בני אדם קשין).</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S02236">
<head-word>קְשֵׁי</head-word>
<head-word>קְשֵׁה</head-word>
<head-word>קְשָׁא</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be hard, difficult</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Deut. I, 17. Ib. XV, 18; a. e.—Yoma 28
<sup>b</sup> קָשׁוּ משמשא are harder (on the eye) &c., v. שַׁבְרִירֵי; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to find a thing difficult to understand, to object, argue against, dispute</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ter. V, 43
<sup>c</sup> bot. ר' סימון קַשְׁיְיתָהּ … קיימה R. Simon argued against it (refuted it), but R. Ba. … proved it to be correct. Y. Kidd. III, 64
<sup>c</sup> top [read:] לא כבר קְשׁוּנְתָּהּ הרי עולם לא כבר קַשְׁיְתָהּ וכ' have not mountains of the world (great scholars) disputed it? did not R. El. dispute it in the presence of &c.; Y. Ned. VIII, 40
<sup>d</sup> sq. (corr. acc.). B. Kam. 66
<sup>b</sup> האי מילתא ק' בה רבה לרב וכ' Rabbah argued this difficulty before R. Joseph for twenty-two years, and it was not solved; Keth. 42
<sup>b</sup> האי … קְשָׁאֵי רבה ורב וכ' Rabbah and R. Joseph discussed this difficulty &c.—Part. קָשֵׁי; f. קַשְׁיָא, q. v.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to get old</italic>, v. 
<xref rid="S02267">קְשַׁשׁ II</xref>.</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>קַשֵּׁי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be in pain of travailing</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Gen. XXXV, 17 בקַשָּׁיוּתָהּ (not בקַשְׁיוּ'). Targ. O. ib. 16 (Y. II 
<italic>Ithpa.</italic>).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to perplex</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pes. 78
<sup>b</sup> מתניתן קַשִּׁיתֵיה וכ' the Mishnah perplexed him; why does it read &c.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Af.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אַקְשֵׁי, אַקְשֵׁה</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to harden, make difficult</italic>.</definition>
<notes>. Targ. Ex. VII, 3. Targ. II Kings II, 10. Targ. I Kings XII, 4. Targ. Ps. XCV, 8; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be hard on, press heavily</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Cant. R. to II, 16 כד הוה צערא קשי עלוי … וכד הוה מַקְשֵׁי וכ' when his suffering was severe, he said, God the faithful, but when it was severer on him than necessary &c.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to argue against, object, dispute</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Job VI, 6 Ms. Var. מדלית מַקְשׁה עליה when there is none to dispute it.—Yeb. 77
<sup>a</sup> top א' להו דואג כל הני קושייתא Doeg brought up before them all those arguments. Y. Yoma I, 38
<sup>d</sup> bot. עד דאת מַקְשֵׁי … קְשַׁיְיתָהּ על וכ' (not קשייתא) instead of offering objection against R. J., rather offer it against &c.; a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Ithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִתְקֵשֵּׁי, </binyan-form>
<binyan-name>Ithpe.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִיקְּשֵׁי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be in pain of travailing</italic>.</definition>
<notes>. Targ. Y. II Gen. XXXV, 16, v. supra.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be difficult, perplexing</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 40
<sup>a</sup> ומִיקְּשֵׁה היא דאיקשי לך וכ' (Rashi דקשיא) it was perplexing to thee, and thou didst reverse it.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="S02237">
<head-word>קְשִׁי</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) = קוֹשִׁי, 
<italic>hardness, stiffness; difficulty</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tanḥ. Sh’laḥ ed. Bub., supplement 14 אל תבט בק' ערפם look not at their stiffneckedness; Num. R. s. 16 end בקשה (corr. acc.).—
<plural-form>Pl. קְשָׁיִין</plural-form>. Sifré Deut. 305 אין חבר נקנה אלא בקשי ק' a friend can be acquired only with the greatest difficulty.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S02238">
<head-word>קָשֵׁי</head-word>
<head-word>(קְשֵׁי)</head-word>
<head-word>קַשְׁיָא</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> c. = h. קָשֶׁה, 
<italic>hard, strong, heavy, difficult</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Ex. VI, 9. Targ. Y. ib. 12. Targ. Gen. XLIX, 7. Targ. Is. XIX, 4. Targ. Ps. LX, 5; a. fr.—Targ. Y. Num. VIII, 4 מינא ק' something hard to understand (v. Num. R. s. 15, quot. s. v. קָשָׁה 
<italic>Nithpa.</italic>).—Yoma 28
<sup>b</sup> ק' משימשא is harder to bear &c., v. זוֹהֲמָא. Ib. 29
<sup>a</sup> ק' 
<pgbrk id="pg1431" />,מקייטא v. קַיְטָא. B. Mets. 85
<sup>a</sup> ק' יומא דמיטרא וכ' a rainy day (preventing people from pursuing their vocations) is as hard as the day of judgment; Taan. 8
<sup>b</sup> קשה (Rashi קשי); a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. קָשִׁין, קָשַׁיָּיא, קָשָׁן; קַשְׁיָין, קַשְׁיָיתָא</plural-form>. Targ. I Sam. XX, 10. Targ. II Sam. III, 39. Targ. II Esth. IV, 1; a. fr.—Y. Sabb. VIII, 11
<sup>b</sup>. Koh. R. to III, 2 מן קל מיליא קַשְׁיָיאתָא וכ' on account of the hard things that I hear &c.; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S02239">
<head-word>קַשְׁיָא</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced.) 
<italic>difficult, open to objection; unanswerable objection; contradiction</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Erub. 13
<sup>a</sup> הא גופא ק' וכ' this in itself is a contradiction; you said, R. I. did not say such a thing, which implies that this opinion is to be rejected, and then you said, this opinion is the adopted rule. Ib. ק' שימוש אשימוש there is a contradiction between the two narratives of R. Meir’s ministrations; ק' אסרה אאסרה there is a contradiction between the relations concerning the teacher who forbade it; שימוש אשימוש לא ק' וכ' there is no contradiction between the two relations concerning the ministrations, (for I may say.) first he went &c.; אלא אסרה אאסרה ק' ק' but between the relations as to who prohibited it, is there not a contradiction? There 
<italic>is</italic> a contradiction (it remains unanswered). Ber. 22
<sup>b</sup> לא ק' וכ' there is no contradiction (between the two traditions): the one speaks of a case where the thing is possible, the other &c. Sabb. 22
<sup>b</sup> ק' the argument (of R. Papa) is unanswerable. Y. ib. XII, end, 13
<sup>d</sup> וק' על דרבן וכ' and this is an argument against the opinion of Rabban G.; a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S02242">
<head-word>קַשְׁיוּת</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (preced. wds.) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (sub. עורף) 
<italic>stiffneckedness</italic>; (sub. לב) 
<italic>hard-heartedness</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Taan. 6
<sup>a</sup>, v. מַלְקוֹשׁ. Lam. R. introd. (R. Joḥ. 1) (play on מקשת אסרו, Is. XXII, 3) מקַשְׁיוּתָם נמסרו וכ' for their stubbornness they were given over to the governments. Gen. R. s. 53 (ref. to רבה קשת, Gen. XXI, 20) רָבָה וקַשְׁיוּתוֹ עמו he (Ishmael) grew, and his stubbornness with him; [anoth. vers.] רבה וקשיותו אמו he grew, and the cause of his renitence was his mother (who encouraged him in his sinful ways); a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>erection, sensual desire</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ib. s. 98 (play on קשתו, Gen. XLIX, 24) ק' שנִתְקַשֵּׁיתָה וכ' the sensual desire which seized thee when thou wast with thy mistress.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S02243">

<sense>
<number>1)</number>

<number>—2)</number>

<italic>stiffneckedness, renitence</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ber. VII, 11
<sup>b</sup> bot. עד כדון את בקַשְׁיוּתָךְ dost thou still persist in thy renitence?; Koh. R. to VII, 11. Y. Peah VII, 20
<sup>b</sup> top. Esth. R. introd. (play on ממקשי, Job XXXIV, 30) מן קַשְׁיוּתֵיהֶן וחיביהן וכ' for the renitence and the guilt of men who do not the will of the Creator; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="S02244">
<head-word>קַשִּׁיט</head-word>

<head-word>קְשִׁ'</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>

<entry id="S02264">

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) [
<italic>to strengthen</italic>, v. Gen. XXX, 41, sq.</definition>
<notes>] 
<italic>to join, knot, tie; to fold</italic>. Sabb. VII, 2 הקוֹשֵׁר והמתיר he that makes a knot or unties it. Y. ib. 10
<sup>c</sup> שהיו קוֹשְׁרִין וכ' they knotted the ropes (of the Tabernacle). Ib. נפסק היה קוֹשְׁרוֹ when a thread was broken (in weaving), one knotted it. Y. Gitt. VIII, end, 49
<sup>d</sup> אפי' קושר וכ' even if he folds (the document) up, and then has it signed. Ib. בשׁקְשָׁרוֹ וחתמו וכ' when he folded it and had it signed inside; a. fr.—Trnsf. 
<italic>a</italic>) (cmp. חָרַז) 
<italic>to compose and arrange</italic> (
<italic>a funeral song or eulogy</italic>). Y. Yoma I, 38
<sup>b</sup> קָשְׁרוּ הספידו they arranged his eulogy. Lam. R. introd. (R. Joḥ. </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>, v. 
<xref rid="M01986">מִסְפֵּד</xref>; a. fr.—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>conceive, form an affection</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pesik. B’shallaḥ, p. 80
<sup>a</sup> הוא קושר לו אהבה וכ' he acquires love and affection for him; Gen. R. s. 54; Yalk. Prov. 954; a. e.—Part. pass. קָשׁוּר; f. קְשׁוּרָה &c. Y. Nidd. I, 49
<sup>b</sup> top אילו יהושע שהיה ק' למשה וכ' a Joshua who was tied to Moses (his constant attendant) could not have spoken so (that Moses had not said a certain thing), and he says so (of R. Jeremiah)? Erub. II, 1 קְשׁוּרוֹת, v. נָתַר. Y. Yeb. XVI, 15
<sup>d</sup> top, v. הֶסְפֵּד; a. e.</notes></sense></senses>

<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> same, esp. 
<italic>to fold a document</italic>, to write a portion and fold it and have witnesses signed on the fold, and so continue to the end of the document.</definition>
<notes> Y. Gitt. l. c. היה מְקַשֵּׁר ראשון ראשון if he folded up the signatures one by one; a. e.—Part. pass. מְקוּשָּׁר. מק' (גט) 
<italic>a folded document</italic>, opp. פָּשׁוּט. B. Bath. X, 1 גט פשוט … ומק' עדיו אחוריו a plain document has its signatures of witnesses inside, a folded one, on its back. Ib. 160
<sup>a</sup> sq. (ref. to Jer. XXXII, 44) וכתוב … וחתום זה מק' ‘and write the deed’, this refers to the plain document, ‘and sign’, this means the folded document; Y. ib. X, beg. 17
<sup>c</sup> (ref. to Jer. ib. 1</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition />
<notes> את החתום זה המק' ואת הגלוי זה הפשוט שבמק' ‘the sealed’ means the folded, ‘and the open’ means the plain document which goes with the folded. Ib. bot. טופס שטרות מְקוּשָּׁרוֹת וכ' such is the formula of folded documents; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<sup>c</sup> top משיעשה קשרין קשרין when it gets full of knotty excrescences; ib. מכיון שנקשר בו קשר וכ' R. S. to Shebi. l. c. (ed. שנִתְקַשֵּׁר) as soon as the uppermost protuberance is formed, it begins to dry up.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<sup>b</sup>. Nidd. 31

I, 31) מלך … ר' אחת וכ' when a human king builds a palace, he casts one (examining) glance at the upper stories and another at the lower; אבל … ר' אחת but the Lord casts one look at both; העוה"ז … ר' אחת with one glance the Lord surveyed this world and the world to come; Yalk. ib. 15 בר'. Lam. R. to V, 1 ר' מרחוק 
<italic>raah</italic> is used for looking from a distance, v. הַבָּטָה; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. רְאִיּוֹת, רְאִיּיוֹת</plural-form>. Ex. R. s. 3 (ref. to ראה ראיתי, Ex. III, 7) ואני רואה שתי ר', v. רָאָה; Tanḥ. Sh’moth 20; Ex. R. s. 42; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (sub. קרי, דם, זיבה &c.) 
<italic>feeling, affection, attack</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Zab. I, 1 הרואה ר' אחת של זוב he who has had one attack of gonorrhœa. Ib. 6 מקצת הר' מהיום וכ' one of the attacks on one day, and another on the day after; a. fr.—
<italic>Pl.</italic> as ab. Nidd. 37
<sup>b</sup> מטמיא בר' כבימים becomes unclean by a certain number of attacks (even if they all be on one day) as well as by a certain number of days. B. Kam. 24
<sup>a</sup> קירבה רְאִיּוֹתֶיהָ if she had her attacks at short intervals; ריחקה ר' at long intervals; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> (with ref. to Ex. XXIII, 17) 
<italic>appearance in the Temple, pilgrimage</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥag. I, 1 הכל חייבים בר' וכ' all (males) are under obligation to appear in the Temple, except &c. Ib. 2 הר' מעה כסף the pilgrim’s burnt-offering must be worth a m’ʿah of silver (v. רֵאָיוֹן). Ib. 7
<sup>a</sup> (ref. to ראיון, Peah I, 1) רְאִיַּית פנים בעזרה it means the appearance in the Temple (has no limits, you may visit the Temple during the festive season as often as you desire); (another opinion) ראיית פנים בקרבן it means the visit connected with a sacrifice (and you must offer a sacrifice as often as you appear); Y. Peah I, 15
<sup>a</sup> bot. [read:] מתניתן בר' פנים אבל ר' קרבן יש לה שיעור the Mishnah in saying that 
<italic>reayon</italic> has no limits refers to the number of appearances, but as regards the visit attended with sacrifice, it has a limit (as to the minimum value of the sacrifice). Ḥag. 6
<sup>a</sup> עולה … עולת ר' הואי the burnt-offering which the Israelites brought in the desert (Ex. XXIV, 15) was the offering of appearance before God; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup>, a. e. אין הנדון דומה לר' the case under discussion is not parallel to the evidence (the case which you cite is not analogous). Ber. 2
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. אע"פ שאין ר' וכ', v. זֵכֶר; a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. רַאֲיוֹת</plural-form>. Snh. l. c. כל ר' שיש לך וכ' whatever new evidences you may have, you must produce within thirty days. Y. Shebu. VI, 37

<entry id="T00031">
<head-word>רֹאשׁ</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>head, point; beginning, heading; main thing, principal</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. IV, 1 הוציא את רֹאשׁוֹ וכ' if the embryo put forth its head, although it withdrew it again. Gen. R. s. 71, beg., v. סוֹף. Midr. Prov. to I, 7 ר' הפרק ר' המסכתא ר' הפרשה the heading of a chapter, of a treatise, of a section.—ר' החדש, ר' השנה &c., v. respective determinants.—Meg. 12
<sup>b</sup> קופץ בר', v. הֶדְיוֹט.—בת ר', v. בַּת II.—Sifra B’ḥuck., Par. 2, ch. VIII (ref. to יען וביען, Lev. XXVI, 43) וכי ר' בר' פרעתי מהם וכ' did I collect from them full amount for full amount? did I not collect only one hundredth of their sins before me? Snh. 3
<sup>a</sup> sq. ממון שאינו משתלם בר' הוא an indemnity not for the exact amount (more or less). B. Kam. 65
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Lev. V, 24) ממון … בר' מוסיף חומש וכ' where the indemnity is for the full amount (and no more), the fine of a fifth is added, but where it is not for the exact amount (but more) &c.; a. v. fr.—מֵר' from the beginning, 
<italic>over again</italic>. Ab. Zar. 3
<sup>a</sup> תנה לנו מר' וכ' give us it (the Law) over again, and we will observe it.—
<plural-form>Pl. רָאשִׁים, רָאשִׁין</plural-form>. Ḥull. II, 2 השוחט שני ר' כאחד if one cuts two heads at one time. Ḥag. 13
<sup>a</sup> רָאשֵׁי פרקים, v. פֶּרֶק; a. fr.—Trnsf. 
<italic>a</italic>) 
<italic>chief, magistrate, leader, president</italic>. Y. R. Hash. I, 57
<sup>b</sup> bot. ר' גדר היה וכ' it was the chief magistrate of Gadara &c., v. רֵאשִׁית; Bab. ib. 22
<sup>a</sup> שזפר ראשָׁהּ וכ' Sh. the chief &c. Sabb. 33
<sup>b</sup>; Ber. 63
<sup>b</sup>, v. מְדַבֵּר. Ib. 57
<sup>b</sup>, v. יְשִׁיבָה. Y. Hor. III, 48
<sup>b</sup> bot. ר' משמר the chief of the Temple guard; ר' בית אב the chief of a priestly family. Ib. [read:] ר' וזקן ר' קודם שאינו ר' וכ' as between the chief (the Nasi, of the academy) and an elder (scholar), the chief has the precedence, for none can be chief unless he has been an elder; a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. as ab. Ib. משה הקדים ר' לזקנים</plural-form> Moses placed the chiefs before the elders (Deut. XXIX, 9). Gen. R. s. 61 כולהון ראשי אומות הן they are all (names derived from) tribal chiefs (v. לוּפָר, a. correct citation acc.); a. fr.—
<italic>b</italic>) 
<italic>crossbeam</italic>. Neg. XIII, 2, v. פָּתִין.—
<italic>Pl.</italic> as ab. Ib. נראה בר' Bab. ed. (Mish. ed. 
<italic>sing.</italic>) if the leprous spot appeared on the crossbeams.—
<italic>c</italic>) ר' תּוֹר (Chaldaism) [
<italic>ox-head</italic>,] 
<italic>triangle, wedge</italic>. Kel. XVIII, 2 כיצד … ר' ת' how is a piece of furniture with an arched top-piece measured? By drawing an equilateral triangle circumscribing the curve. Kil. II, 7 היה ר' ת' חטים וכ' if a triangular point of a wheat field is wedged in a barley field. Ib. III, 3. B. Bath. 62
<sup>a</sup> (if the seller defined the limits of his field by describing one long side and one short side) ויקנה כנגד ר' ת' why not let the buyer have possession of an ‘ox-head’, i.e. draw a trapezoid with the two unequal sides?—
<italic>Pl.</italic> רָאשֵׁי תוֹרִין. Y. Erub. I, 19
<sup>c</sup> bot.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<plural-form>Pl. רִאשׁוֹנוֹת</plural-form>. Ber. 13

<sup>a</sup>, v. מָצָא; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>teacher</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 63
<sup>b</sup> יאמרו הרב בכעס וכ' they will say, the teacher (the Lord) is angry, and the disciple (Moses) is angry, what is to become of Israel? Ib. כל תלמיד … רבו וכ' a student with whom his teacher is angry for the first time, and who keeps silence. Eduy. I, 3, v. לָשׁוֹן. Ab. I, 16 עשה לך רב וכ' get thyself a teacher, and be relieved of doubt. R. Hash. II, 9 רַבִּי ותלמידי רבי וכ' my teacher and my pupil; my teacher in wisdom &c.; v. רַבִּי.—M. Kat. 9
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. למדתנו רַבֵּינוּ thou, our teacher, hast taught us; v. רַבֵּנוּ; a. v. fr.—Esp. רַב 
<italic>Rab, a</italic>) title of the Babylonian Amoraim. Pes. 52
<sup>b</sup>; a. v. fr.—בי רב the school of, v. בֵּי.—
<italic>b</italic>) surname of Abba Arekha, the founder of the academy of Sura in Babylonia (v. Graetz, Gesch. d. Jud.
<sup>1</sup> IV, p. 312, sq.; Fr. M’bo, p. 122
<sup>b</sup>). Ḥull. 95
<sup>b</sup> כולהו שני דרב וכ' as long as Rab lived, R. Joḥ. addressed his letters to Babylonia, ‘to our teacher in Babylonia.’ Ab. Zar. 10
<sup>b</sup> אדרכן שמשיה לרב A. (a Parthian ruler) attended (associated with) Rab. Y. Peah VI, 19
<sup>c</sup> רב כד נחת לתמן when Rab came down to Babylonia. Erub. 50
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. רב תנא הוא ופליג Rab is a Tannai and has a right to differ (with other Tannaim). Nidd. 24
<sup>b</sup>, a. fr. הלכתא כרב וכ', v. אִיסּוּרָא; a. v. fr.—ספרא דבי רב, ספרי דבי רב, v. סִפְרָא.—
<plural-form>Pl. רַבּוֹת</plural-form> (only with suffix). Taan. 7
<sup>a</sup>, a. e. מרַבּוֹתַי, v. לָמַד. Shebu. 47
<sup>a</sup> רַבּוֹתֵינוּ שבבבל וכ' ‘our teachers in Babylonia’ means Rab and Samuel. Y. Gitt. VII, 48
<sup>d</sup> top ורבותינו אמרו and our teachers said; מנו רבותינו וכ' who are meant by ‘our teachers’? Ib., a. e. בשלשה … רבותיני on three occasions R. Judah (with his court) is quoted as ‘our teachers.’ Y. Sabb. V, end, 7
<sup>c</sup> רבותינו שבגולה our teachers in the diaspora (Babylonia, v. supra); Y. Bets. II, 61
<sup>c</sup> bot. Y. Meg. I, 70
<sup>d</sup> כתבו אגרת ושלחו לרבותינו שהן וכ' they (Mordecai and Esther) wrote a letter addressed ‘to our teachers (in Palestine) that be’, saying to them &c.; a. fr.—
<italic>Fem.</italic> רַבָּה 
<italic>mistress</italic>. Ruth R. to II, 5 רַבָּתָהּ וכ' her mistress (Naomi) &c., v. רָפָה.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
